note.explanation: An empirical formula shows the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms in a compound. It does not always show the actual number of atoms in a molecule.
note.simple: Think of an empirical formula as the smallest whole-number ratio of the atoms.
note.checkQuestion: What is the empirical formula of C₆H₁₂?
note.title: Empirical Formula
steps: Find the greatest common factor of 6 and 12: it is 6.

mcqs.stem: What is the empirical formula of C₄H₈?
rationales: Correct: dividing both subscripts by 4 gives the simplest ratio, CH₂.
Incorrect: C₂H₄ can still be simplified by dividing both subscripts by 2.
Incorrect: C₂H₆ does not have the same atom ratio as C₄H₈.
Incorrect: C₃H₆ does not have the same atom ratio as C₄H₈.

mcqs.stem: Which is the empirical formula of hydrogen peroxide, H₂O₂?
rationales: Correct: dividing both subscripts by 2 gives HO.
Incorrect: H₂O₂ is the molecular formula, not the simplest ratio.
Incorrect: H₂O has a different ratio of hydrogen to oxygen.
Incorrect: OH₂ has the same atom ratio as H₂O, not hydrogen peroxide.

mcqs.stem: A molecule has the formula C₆H₆. What is its empirical formula?
rationales: Correct: dividing both subscripts by 6 gives CH.
Incorrect: C₆H₆ is the molecular formula and can be simplified.
Incorrect: C₂H₃ is not the simplest ratio obtained by dividing 6 and 6 by a common factor.
Incorrect: C₃H₃ can still be simplified to CH.

mcqs.stem: Which compound has the same empirical and molecular formula?
rationales: Correct: the 2:1 ratio in H₂O cannot be reduced to a smaller whole-number ratio.
Incorrect: HO is not the formula of water.
Incorrect: H₂O₂ simplifies to HO.
Incorrect: H₄O₂ simplifies to H₂O.

options: The actual number of atoms in a molecule
The simplest whole-number ratio of atoms
The number of molecules in one mole
mcqs.stem: What does an empirical formula show?
rationales: Incorrect: the empirical formula does not necessarily show the actual number of atoms in a molecule.
Correct: it represents the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms in the compound.
Incorrect: an empirical formula does not give an atom's mass.
Incorrect: the number of molecules in one mole is not given by an empirical formula.

mcqs.stem: Which is the simplest formula showing the ratio of calcium ions to fluoride ions in calcium fluoride?
rationales: Correct: CaF₂ shows the simplest 1:2 ratio of calcium to fluoride ions.
Incorrect: Ca₂F₂ can be simplified to CaF and does not show the correct ratio.
Incorrect: CaF gives a 1:1 ratio instead of the correct 1:2 ratio.
Incorrect: Ca₂F gives a 2:1 ratio instead of the correct 1:2 ratio.

written.text: Give two examples of the compounds which have same empirical and molecular formulas.

rubric.why: One valid example is needed to show a compound whose formula cannot be simplified.
A second valid example completes the requested pair.

modelAnswer: Water: H₂O cannot be simplified to a smaller whole-number ratio.
Ammonia: NH₃ cannot be simplified to a smaller whole-number ratio.
Therefore, examples are water (H₂O) and ammonia (NH₃).

written.text: Find out the molecular formula of a compound whose empirical formula is CH₂O and its molar mass is 180.

rubric.why: The empirical formula mass is needed to find the multiplier.
rubric.description: Calculates the empirical formula mass as 30.

rubric.why: The molecular formula must use the multiplier for every subscript.
rubric.how: Show 180 ÷ 30 = 6 and multiply the empirical formula subscripts by 6.

modelAnswer: n = molar mass ÷ empirical formula mass = 180 ÷ 30 = 6.

written.text: Different compounds will never have the same molecule formula but they can have the same empirical formula. Explain
written.finalAnswer: Different compounds can have the same simplest atom ratio but different actual numbers of atoms; therefore, they may share an empirical formula while having different molecular formulas.

rubric.why: The definition of empirical formula is central to explaining the statement.
rubric.description: Explains that an empirical formula gives a simplest ratio.
rubric.how: State that it shows the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms.

rubric.why: The distinction from a molecular formula explains why formulas can differ.
rubric.description: Distinguishes the actual atom count from the simplest ratio.
rubric.how: Explain that a molecular formula shows the actual number of atoms in a molecule.

rubric.why: A textbook example supports the explanation.
rubric.description: Gives benzene and its molecular formula.

rubric.why: The comparison shows two distinct molecular formulas reducing to one empirical formula.
rubric.description: Gives acetylene and identifies the shared empirical formula.
rubric.how: State that acetylene, C₂H₂, also simplifies to CH.

modelAnswer: An empirical formula shows the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms, but a molecular formula shows the actual number of atoms in a molecule.
Benzene has molecular formula C₆H₆ and empirical formula CH.
Acetylene has molecular formula C₂H₂ and empirical formula CH.
Thus, different compounds can have the same empirical formula but different molecular formulas.

written.text: The chemical formula for sand is SiO₂ but the sand does not exist in the form of discrete molecules like H₂O. How has its formula been determined keeping in view its structure?
written.finalAnswer: SiO₂ gives the simplest 1:2 ratio of silicon to oxygen atoms in the structure of sand; it is an empirical formula, not the formula of a discrete molecule.

rubric.why: Recognising the structure explains why a molecular formula is not used.
rubric.description: States that sand is not made of discrete molecules.
rubric.how: Explain that its atoms form an extended structure.

rubric.why: The elements in the formula must be identified correctly.
The elements in the formula must be identified correctly.
The final formula expresses the simplest ratio in the structure.
rubric.description: Gives the simplest silicon-to-oxygen ratio and formula.
rubric.how: State that SiO₂ represents a 1:2 ratio.

modelAnswer: Sand has an extended structure and does not exist as discrete SiO₂ molecules.
Its formula represents the ratio of silicon atoms to oxygen atoms in that structure.
Therefore, SiO₂ is its empirical formula.

examTips: The board may ask for the definition of empirical formula or ask you to distinguish it from a molecular formula.
For a numerical question, first find the empirical formula mass, then divide the molar mass by it to get the multiplier.
To get full marks in a formula calculation, show the mass calculation, the multiplier, and the multiplication of every subscript.
A short explanation may ask why different compounds can have the same empirical formula; include a suitable example such as benzene and acetylene.

hints: Choose compounds whose formulas cannot be reduced to a simpler ratio.
Water is one example from your textbook; choose another compound whose atom subscripts have no common factor greater than 1.
yourTurn.question: Give two examples of the compounds which have same empirical and molecular formulas.
solution: In water, H₂O, the subscripts 2 and 1 have no common factor greater than 1.
In ammonia, NH₃, the subscripts 1 and 3 have no common factor greater than 1.
So the empirical and molecular formulas are the same for both compounds.

hints: Find the mass of one empirical formula unit, CH₂O.
Divide 180 by that mass; multiply each subscript in CH₂O by the result.
yourTurn.question: Find out the molecular formula of a compound whose empirical formula is CH₂O and its molar mass is 180.
solution: n = molar mass ÷ empirical formula mass = 180 ÷ 30 = 6.

steps.why: This is the molecular formula given for hydrogen peroxide in your textbook.
steps.text: Molecular formula of hydrogen peroxide = H₂O₂.

steps.why: Both subscripts have a common factor of 2, so the ratio can be reduced.
steps.text: Divide both subscripts by 2: H₂O₂ → HO.

steps.why: HO is the simplest whole-number ratio of hydrogen to oxygen atoms.
steps.text: Empirical formula of hydrogen peroxide = HO.

explain.title: Meaning of empirical formula
explain.body: Empirical Formula of a compound shows the simplest whole number ratio of atoms present in that compound.

explain.title: Ionic compounds
explain.body: All the ionic compounds are represented by their empirical formulas. These formulas show the simplest ratio present between their ions. For example, CaF₂ shows the ratio present between calcium and fluoride ions in its crystal.

explain.title: Empirical and molecular formulas
explain.body: For covalent chemical compounds, which exist as molecules, the empirical formulas may be different from their molecular formulas. Hydrogen peroxide is H₂O₂ as a molecular formula and HO as an empirical formula.

explain.title: Sometimes they are the same
explain.body: For water, the molecular formula and the empirical formula are both the same i.e. H₂O because there does not exist any minimum ratio between hydrogen and oxygen atoms.

explain.title: Different compounds can share an empirical formula
explain.body: Since an empirical formula does not tell us the actual number of atoms present in that compound, rather it represents the simplest ratio between atoms, it is possible that some compounds may have the same empirical formula. For example, both benzene (C₆H₆) and acetylene (C₂H₂) have the same empirical formula CH.

mistakes: Do not confuse a molecular formula, which gives the actual number of atoms in a molecule, with an empirical formula, which gives the simplest ratio.
Do not stop at a formula that can still be simplified; divide all subscripts by their greatest common factor.
When finding a molecular formula from an empirical formula, multiply every subscript by the same whole-number multiplier.
Do not describe an ionic compound's empirical formula as a count of discrete molecules; it shows the simplest ratio of ions.
